title: MV How can I create a fourth vehicle capable of moving over land and water, but NOT mountains?

posts.author: Egar_Kresreb
posts.body:
First of all, while I've read some of the other MV-related threads on here before, I have only made an account today. Seeing as how this is my first post, please forgive me if I put this in the wrong spot.
Anyway, I'm using RPG Maker MV, and I was wondering if there's a way to make a fourth vehicle that works exactly like a ship/boat, but it's able to go on land as well as water. In my game, I wanted to be able to give my characters access to basically the black chocobos of the Final Fantasy games. The only difference is that my creature is a
lizard
, not a bird, so I don't want it to look like it's flying.
I put this in plugin requests because I figured that there's probably a plugin already out there somewhere that can do what I need. I
do
have pretty much all of the Yanfly plugins, but I don't know what they all do, so maybe I've had what I need sitting under my nose this whole time. I would like a solution that requires little or no coding on my part, since I know absolutely nothing about Javascript. Also, please note that I cannot just change the settings for any of the three already existing vehicles in the game. I'm already using all three of them, and cannot remove/change those ones.

There's not really any such thing as a suite of plugins that doesn't work with another suite of plugins.
You get plugin conflicts by having two plugins that try to change the same thing, not from having plugins by different authors in your project.

Also, after you make changes, are you saving your project and starting a new play test game? Not loading a save?

You can't, unless you read the code to determine the format of the save game and edit in all of the information needed by the plugin.
Really, that's not a good thing to get used to because many database changes, installing/changing/altering plugins, adding notetags, all won't be reflected when loading a save game.
So you should get yourself accustomed to starting a fresh game whenever you make changes.

posts.author: ATT_Turan
posts.body:
Egar_Kresreb said:
I guess Yanfly's plugins don't do that or something.
Click to expand...
Depending on which ones you're talking about, Yanfly's are a major offender in this area - he almost never directly references any notetags from the database, he always loads them and attaches them to game objects.
So if your objects (actors, independent items, etc.) were created in a game version that didn't have the notetags and their loading procedure, they won't get added when you install the plugin.
